cards.text: Paul, an apostle, is writing to the believers in Rome (Romans 1:1, 7). He just finished a heavy one: no one will be justified in God's sight by works of the law (Romans 3:20), and baker, I read that and almost crawled back into my old junk drawer. Then Paul turns it all around: "But now, apart from the law, the righteousness of God has been revealed".

cards.question: True or false: Paul says the Law and the Prophets point to this righteousness of God.

cards.text: So if it comes apart from the law, how does anybody get this righteousness from God? And no, friend, it doesn't come with a bigger mustache. I checked.

cards.question: Paul says the righteousness of God has been revealed apart from the law. How does it come to people?

cards.text: And it comes to all who believe. Paul says, "There is no distinction," and then he gives the reason why.

cards.question: Paul says there's no distinction between people, because all have ___ and fall short of the glory of God.

cards.text: Friend, I stand on a gold base in a chef's hat THIS tall, and I STILL fall short. But Paul keeps going: they are justified freely by His grace.

cards.question: True or false: Paul saying people are justified "freely" means they have to pay God back later.

cards.text: Mother Miller paid a whole quarter for me at a bakery going out of business, and I thought THAT was a bargain. This is FREE, and Paul says it comes through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus.
Paul says God presented Jesus as an atoning sacrifice in His blood through faith. And before this, in His forbearance, God had passed over the sins committed beforehand.

cards.question: Why did God present Jesus as an atoning sacrifice?

answers.text: To show the law was a mistake
To show sin no longer matters

cards.question: Paul says God did this to show His righteousness at the present time. What two things does it let God do at once?

answers.text: Stay just and justify the one with faith
Stay strict and overlook every sin
Stay patient and set the law aside

cards.text: Then Paul asks, "Where, then, is boasting?" Baker, after a perfect batch I get louder than Mags, so I'm a little nervous about where this is going.

cards.question: Paul asks where boasting is. What's his answer?

answers.text: It is earned by good works
It is fine in small amounts

cards.question: Paul says boasting is shut out by the principle not of ___ but of ___.

cards.text: Paul sums it up: "a man is justified by faith apart from works of the law." The dead batteries I shared that drawer with argued for YEARS over who had the most charge left, and this one verse would've shut the whole drawer up.

cards.question: Paul asks whether God is the God of Jews only. True or false: Paul says He is the God of Gentiles too.

cards.text: Paul says that's because there is only one God. And that one God will justify both the circumcised and the uncircumcised.

cards.question: God will justify the circumcised by faith and the uncircumcised through ___ faith.
Paul asks, "Do we, then, nullify the law by this faith?" True or false: his answer is yes, faith does away with the law.
